correctness.rationale: For J(N,k) endpoints distance d>=1, every shortest path must remove the d distinct A\B elements and insert the d B\A elements once each, so path states are pairs of permutations (sigma,tau), with (d!)^2 states. Holding neighboring intermediate vertices fixed yields exactly four choices at each i: swap i and i+1 in either coordinate, or both; these form edge-disjoint K4, with no inter-index triangles. The Cayley graph has degree 3(d-1), (d-1)(d!)^2/4 maximal four-cliques and (d-1)(d!)^2 triangles. Synchronized fixed bubble-comparator schedule sorts both orderings in <=binom(d,2) steps; inversion reversal in one component gives the matching lower bound, and vertex transitivity makes radius equal to diameter. Independent directly reconstructed paths and edge adjacencies for d<=4, confirming (1,4,36,576) states and (0,1,3,6) diameters; the quantified all-d proof is combinatorial, not extrapolated from tests.
